why: The authors' repository is cloned and self-contained: it ships both a Python implementation (py/LO_K_means.py, py/run.py) and a C++ implementation, plus the exact datasets used in the claim contract (data/Iris.txt, wine_quality.txt, news20_2000_1089.txt, predict.txt, yeast.txt). K-means needs no trained weights, and the only Python dependency is numpy, which is trivially installable on Python 3.12. The match target (C1: Iris K=5, 20 random inits, Min-D-LO) is directly produced by the released entrypoint, so the authors' own code can be run first.

feasibility.est_runtime_on_this_machine: Well under 2 minutes: install numpy (seconds), then 20 Iris fits of K-means + Min-D-LO at <1 ms each, plus the same at K-means baseline for the C1/C2 comparison. The optional C++ path adds one g++ compile (~10-30 s).

compute.basis: Match target is 20 runs of K-means/Min-D-LO on Iris (150x4), each reported at <0.001 s in Table 1; total command time is dominated by the numpy install and an optional C++ compile, so the whole protocol is a couple of minutes at most.
